newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia said under pressure to probe 1984 riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia said under pressure to probe 1984 riots.

text.p: The Indonesian government is under pressure to reopen investigations into riots in Jakarta over 12 years ago but is unlikely to readily respond, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Friday.
"It will be some time before the government could attend to the request to reopen the investigation," Defence Minister Edi Sudradjat was quoted as saying.

Over 200 people gathered at a local mosque on Thursday to commemorate the deaths of at least 18 people killed when police fired on anti-government protesters in the Tanjung Priok port area of Jakarta in 1984.
The secretary-general of the National Commission on Human Rights, Baharuddin Lopa, has said that the riots -- which have never been independently investigated -- will be discussed in December.
Tha Jakarta Post said the commission had received several requests to inquire into the incident in which the government says 18 people were killed.
Human rights groups put the toll at at least 26.
The commission, which was set up in 1993, has differed with the government version of riots in Jakarta in July this year, sparked by a police raid on the office of the Indonesian Democratic Party.
The government has said three people died but the commission has put the death toll at five and says at least 74 others are still missing.
